independent_checks: Finite type hypothesis is separated from arbitrary fibre-product construction.
Nonempty m-dimensional closed-subset axiom does not follow from initial smoothness; dense constructible image U and a closed m-dimensional W meeting U make the general dominance argument valid.

Mixed-dimensional generic intersection dimension is the maximum over surviving irreducible components; the disjoint union P1 and A2 example satisfies the hypotheses and disproves the original unrestricted formula.

Initial geometrically irreducible but nonreduced G need not yield a regular generic-section morphism; the dual-numbers example disproves the unconditional local regularity equivalence. G reduced at its generic point suffices for the stated regular-morphism premise.
Unramifiedness must concern the fibre morphism or incidence morphism j. The standard point-line incidence example disproves the original total-projection ramification locus.

A smooth fibre alone does not ensure smoothness over a nonreduced parameter base. The explicit dual-number parameter example disproves the original bad-locus estimate while leaving the generic smoothness conclusion true.

With smooth P and X, the incidence spaces are reduced and factor through G_red; a common generic-flat open permits the corrected closed bad locus, tangent transversality, quasi-finite fibre estimates and the uniform dimension argument.
Chevalley, generic flatness, regular morphisms and other cited primary statements were actually opened and matched to their uses.
Negative or zero dimension edge cases and nonpure smooth X are explicitly scoped.
The author's unproved generalization plans, missing object, recoverable English transcription omissions and older unresolved manuscript gaps remain distinctly attributed.
